column1: # The SELF container, as three independent open-source projects read or write it.
# Columns: struct, field, offset, size, type, value, note
# read-from: shadPS4@be21649             src/core/loader/elf.h        C++       reader
#            fpPS4@04cefd4               sys/sys_types.pas            Pascal    reader
#            OpenOrbis-PS4-Toolchain@0a1aaf9  scripts/make_fself.py   Python    WRITER
#            prosperity@3475257          tools/pkg_extract/pkg_extract.py  Python  reader
# The fourth arrived after the builder was written and confirms it independently, including
# the two fields whose absence a loader rejected: `if not (flags & 0x800): continue` and
# `idx = (flags >> 20) & 0xFFF`. It also pins something the others leave implicit — the ELF
# begins at `0x20 + segment_count * 0x20`, immediately after the entry table with no padding,
# which is where mkself already puts it.
# **No vendor binary was read to produce this table**, and none may be read to extend it.
# Derivation happens against sources that can be named; what enters the repository is text
# with a header saying where it came from; a generator reads the text rather than the thing
# it was derived from. `titles/` holds packages to check output against - nothing in `tool/`
# may open them. (orbistoun#D181, orbistoun#D182)
# # THE LIMIT THAT MATTERS: this is still the previous console's container
# OpenOrbis is a PS4 toolchain and both readers are PS4-generation loaders. **Nothing here is
# confirmed against current-generation vendor material.** The container is expected to be
# closely related and it is the only lawful starting point available, but every row is
# `IMPLEMENTATIONS` at PS4 level until something current accepts or rejects a file built from it.
# That is not a footnote. This project has been caught believing an emulator-derived fact that
# turned out to describe a different program, and the whole reason `mkself` matters is to
# reach the *current* system loader. A file built from this table is a hypothesis.
# ## What was measured on hardware, and why it does not lift that limit
# On 2026-09-09 obSCEne walked every installed application tree on a current-generation console
# and audited **32 containers**, reporting each one's `ex_info.ptype` before its verdict. The
# split is total and it falls exactly on the fake marker:
#   ptype 0x1 (PTYPE_FAKE)  9 containers   all NINE fixed rows match this table
#   ptype 0x0              23 containers   the same FIVE rows differ, identically, on every one
#   the five:  version 0x10 (table 0x0)      attributes 0x32 (table 0x12)
#              key_type 0x10000301 (0x101)   program_type 0x3 (table 0x1)
#              flags 0x52 (table 0x22)
# **No container that is not marked fake matches this table, and every container that is,
# does.** Nine for nine and twenty-three for twenty-three, with no partial cases in either
# direction.
# ### Four rows *are* confirmed against genuine material, and that was under-recorded
# The five that differ took all the attention. The other four - `mode` 0x1, `endian` 0x1,
# `category` 0x1, `padding3` 0x0 - hold on **all 23 genuine containers as well as all 9 fake
# ones**, and each row now says so in place.
# That is the first confirmation this table has ever had from material this repository could not
# have produced, and it is principle 2 working exactly as written: derived from citable
# previous-generation sources, then checked against current-generation reality, and the rows
# reality settled recorded as settled. Four of nine is a smaller claim than the one withdrawn
# this afternoon and it is the one that survives.
# The simplest explanation is also the one this table's provenance predicts: it was derived from
# **OpenOrbis, a fake-SELF writer**, so it describes what that writer produces. A container
# written by an OpenOrbis-lineage tool agrees with it because of where the rows came from, not
# because a console confirmed them - which is why the `confirmed` verdicts here are round trips
# and the limit above stands.
# ## The confound, stated because an earlier version of this file glossed it
# **Authenticity and container kind are perfectly correlated in this sample.** Every `ptype 0x1`
# container is `PPSA`-shaped - a game title id - and every `ptype 0x0` container is `NPXS`-shaped,
# a system application. There is not one genuine application container on the box, and not one
# fake system one.
# So these five rows may describe *a fake container* or *an application container*, and **this
# measurement cannot tell those apart**. An earlier revision of this section said the limit was
# categorical - "these five rows describe an application container" - and that was reading one
# arm of a confound as the cause. The fake reading is the better-supported of the two, because
# it is what the table's own source wrote and because `ptype` is literally the field the format
# provides for saying so; it is not established, and neither is the other.
# What would separate them is a container that is genuine **and** application-shaped - a real
# retail game - or a fake system-tier one. The console holds neither, so this question is not
# answerable from it and is not being asked of it again.
# One thing the sample does settle about *this* writer: `mkself` emits the same five values at
# every privilege tier, because `Privilege` reaches only `paid` in `self_ex_info`. So within what
# this repository builds, these rows do not encode a tier. That is a fact about the writer, not
# about the platform.
#   measured-by: obscene 048-selfaudit, sweep 20260909-175052, payload leg (REQ-20260909T1605Z-9c40)
#   settles: that no non-fake container on one current-generation console matches these five
#            rows, and that all nine fixed rows hold for fake ones. Does NOT settle whether the
#            five track authenticity or container kind - the sample confounds them.
# ## The magic: settled, and here the confound really is broken
# The five rows above are stuck behind a confound. The **magic** is not, and it is worth being
# clear about why, because it is the one place on this console where the sample separates the two
# things it was asked to.
# A 2x2 cross-census of all 32 containers, magic against `ex_info.ptype`
# (obscene 048-selfaudit, sweep 20260909-184538):
#                     current magic (54 14 F5 EE)   previous magic (4F 15 3D 1D)
#   ptype 0x0                    23                             0
#   ptype 0x1                     7                             2
# **Every genuine container carries the current magic, and none carries the previous one.** The
# reason that is not just "everything on this console is current-generation" is the bottom row:
# the fake population spans **both** values, so carrying the current magic is not something the
# console imposes on whatever is installed. Genuine is 23/0; fake is 7/2. The correlation
# survives having a control group, which is exactly what the five header rows lack.
# So the claim this file used to carry - that a current-generation title's eboot carries the
# *previous* magic, "hardware-confirmed" - is **refuted**, not merely unsupported. Its evidence
# was PPSA02664, which is one of the two gen-4 containers and is `ptype 0x1`: fake.
# ### Both magics are accepted, each on its own delivery route
# The question a default actually turns on is acceptance, and it is now answered for both values -
# separately, because the two are proven on **different routes** and neither on the other's:
#   previous magic  a *package* built with it installs, mounts, loads and executes (worklog 040)
#   current magic   a *native title directory* whose eboot carries it installs, launches and runs
#                   to completion - 292 checks (obscene sweep 20260909-184538)
# The second was measured twice over, which is why it is worth stating: the container was built
# here by `mkself --generation 5`, and then **read back off console storage** by the same probe
# that produced the census above - `/system_ex/app/PPSA99980/eboot.bin`, `magic 0xeef51454`,
# `ptype 0x1`. It is one of the 7 fake/current-magic entries in that 2x2. The cross-census
# already contained this repository's own output as a data point.
# ### And the default still does not move, for a different reason than before
# `selfish wrap` defaults to the previous generation's magic. Until the measurement above that was
# because it was the only value shown to be accepted. It is no longer the only one - so the
# reason has changed, and the default has not.
# **It is now a route decision.** `wrap`'s default serves the *package* path, and the previous
# magic is what is proven there. The current magic is proven on the *native title* path, which
# passes `--generation 5` explicitly and does not consult the default at all. Moving the default
# would put the package path onto a value nothing has accepted **on that path** - and D082 already
# records that the two are different delivery routes rather than two spellings of one.
# What has **not** happened at any point is the default moving on a population. It did not move
# when the population said previous (that claim was withdrawn, and its evidence was a fake
# container), and it did not move when the population turned out to say current, 23 of 23. A
# default turns on what a loader accepts, and the answer differs by route.
#   measured-by: obscene 048-selfaudit, sweep 20260909-184538, payload leg (REQ-20260909T2020Z-8a17)
#                and the eboot leg of the same sweep (REQ-20260909T2125Z-3f9d)
#   settles: that genuine current-generation containers carry the current magic, 23 of 23, with
#            fakes present on both sides as a control; and that a container built here with the
#            current magic is accepted on the native-title route. Does NOT settle what either
#            magic does on the *other* route.
# ## The tail: `header_size - 0x70` survived its first contact with material we did not write
# The layout `[... ex_info 64][npdrm 48]` ending at `header_size` comes from OpenOrbis, a **PS4
# writer**, and is the part of this table no reader could have supplied. On 2026-09-09 the probe
# was changed to report the four `ex_info` scalars unconditionally instead of hiding them behind
# a known-`ptype` test, and read seven containers that were demonstrably not written from this
# table (six system apps under `/system/vsh/app/`, plus `/system_ex/app/FAKE00000/`):
#   ptype      0x0       0x0      0x0       0x0       0x0       0x0      0x0
#   app_version 0x0      0x0      0x0       0x0       0x0       0x0      0x0
#   fw_version 0x48      0x48     0x48      0x48      0x48      0x48     0x48
#   npdrm.type 0x0       0x0      0x0       0x0       0x0       0x0      0x0
# **Seven files of different sizes agreeing exactly on three of four fields is not what a
# misaligned read produces.** Reading the wrong bytes of seven unrelated files gives seven
# unrelated answers; this gives one answer with a single field varying. So the offset is very
# probably right, and what these containers carry is simply a *kind this table does not
# describe*. That is a real result and the first one from material this repository could not
# have produced.
# **The sample later grew from seven to twenty-three and the agreement held**: the 32-container
# census above found `ptype 0x0` and `npdrm.type 0x0` on every non-fake container on the box.
# Twenty-three unrelated files agreeing is further past coincidence than seven was, so the
# offset is right and the reading below stands.
# It is stated as *consistent with* rather than proven, because the alternative was not ruled
# out by measurement - only by argument. `paid` varying per application is what a program
# authority id does; it is also what an offset does.
# Recorded as observed, and **not named**: `ptype` `0x0` is not one of the eight values the
# `ptype` group below lists, and `npdrm.type` `0x0` where the table pins `0x3` reads as *no
# npdrm control block*, which a system container plausibly has no use for. Neither gets a row
# here. Principle 5 - an unexplained value is named `unknown` and left alone, and inventing
# `ptype system = 0x0` from one console's system apps is exactly the guess that principle
# exists to stop.
#   measured-by: obscene 048-selfaudit, sweep 20260909-155928, payload leg (REQ-20260909T1545Z-2d84)
#   settles: nothing about what the values mean. Records that the tail is where this table says
#            it is for seven containers this repository did not write, and that they carry
#            `ptype` 0x0 and no npdrm block.
# # Why three sources, and what each was needed for
# A single reading is a guess with a citation. Two readers gave the shape and one constant.
# The writer gave what neither reader could: **the blocks a loader skips**. A reader walks a
# container to find an ELF and never looks at the metadata; a writer has to put something
# there. Everything from `ex_info` down exists only because a packer was available.
# It also settled two things the readers left open:
#   * bytes 4..7 - shadPS4 names four fields and gives no values, fpPS4 gives `00 01 01 12`
#     as one word, OpenOrbis names them AND gives the values. All three agree.
#   * `0x22` at offset 26 - both readers record "always 0x22" and neither says why. It is
#     computed: `0x2 | (signed_block_count & 0x7) << 4`, with signed_block_count = 2.
# # One genuine disagreement, recorded rather than resolved
# Bytes 8..11. shadPS4 reads `category:u8, program_type:u8, padding1:u16`; OpenOrbis writes a
# single `key_type:u32 = 0x101`. Little-endian those are the same bytes - `01 01 00 00` - so
# the disagreement is in naming, not in layout, and a file built either way is identical.
# Both readings are recorded because neither can be shown wrong from here.
# # How the pieces assemble
#   [self_header 32][entry 32 x N][ELF ehdr + phdrs][pad to 16][ex_info 64][npdrm 48]   <- header_size
#   [meta_block 80 x N][meta_footer 80][signature 256]                                  <- meta_size
#   [segment payloads, each aligned to 16]                                              <- from header_size + meta_size
# **Two entries per segment, not one.** A digest entry carrying one 32-byte digest per
# BLOCK_SIZE block of the segment, then a data entry carrying the segment itself. So
# `segment_count` is twice the number of qualifying program headers, which is the single
# thing most likely to be got wrong by reading the readers alone - neither of them says it,
# because neither has to build one.
# Qualifying program header types: PT_LOAD, PT_SCE_RELRO, PT_SCE_DYNLIBDATA, PT_SCE_COMMENT.
# PT_SCE_VERSION is kept aside as version_data rather than becoming an entry.
# For a fake SELF every digest and the whole signature are zero, which is the same statement
# `meta_block` makes by being 80 zero bytes: nothing here is claiming to be signed.
# # THE MAGIC DIFFERS BY GENERATION, AND EVERY SOURCE ABOVE IS THE OLD ONE
# orbistoun (`crates/orbistoun-elf/src/wrapper.rs`, decision D049, status "observed from real
# material") records two magics for one container:
#     current generation   54 14 F5 EE
#     previous generation  4F 15 3D 1D    <- what this table described, and what mkself emitted
# and notes that both appear inside a single title: bundled modules use the current format,
# substituted stub libraries the older one. Its header size, segment size and layout are
# byte-identical to the rows below, so **only the first four bytes change**.
# This was sitting in a sibling repository the whole time. The header above already said
# "nothing here is confirmed for the current console", which was true and was treated as a
# limit to note rather than a question to go and answer - and the answer was one directory
# across, derived from real material rather than from an emulator. Reading the readers and
# the writer was the right method; not checking who had already done it was not.
# Still absent
# `version_data` handling, and the auth_info path that `make_fself.py` takes when given one.
# An absent row is visible; an invented one is not.
